target: Han sa att han inte hade hunnit.
english: He said he hadn't had time.
tip: In subordinate clause: "att han inte hade hunnit" – inte before verb.

target: Det var kaffe hon ville ha, inte te.
english: It was coffee she wanted, not tea.
tip: Det var kaffe hon ville ha is a cleft: front the key word after Det var to stress it, and som before hon is dropped.

target: Han har inte svarat på mitt mejl ännu, så jag försöker ringa honom imorgon.
english: He hasn't answered my email yet, so I'll try calling him tomorrow.
tip: Svara takes på for the thing answered: svarat på mitt mejl. In Swedish you answer on something.

target: Han tog skeden i vacker hand.
english: He tackled the task gracefully.
tip: Ta skeden i vacker hand literally means take the spoon in a fair hand: grit your teeth and make the best of a hard situation.

target: Som jag förstod det var problemet löst.
english: As I understood it, the problem was solved.
tip: The clause Som jag förstod det comes first, so the verb var lands before problemet. Verb stays in second slot.

target: Hon försäkrade mig om att allt var bra.
english: She assured me that everything was fine.
tip: Försäkra needs om before the clause: försäkrade mig om att. The om is not optional here.

target: Jag har alltid velat besöka norra delen av Sverige.
english: I have always wanted to visit the northern part of Sweden.
tip: Velat is the supine of vilja, to want. After har it becomes har velat, have wanted.

target: Han ser efter barnen.
english: He looks after the children.
tip: Se efter is a particle verb meaning look after; the stressed efter shifts se away from plain see. Han ser efter barnen.

target: Var god och fyll i formuläret.
english: Please fill in the form.
tip: Var god och is a set polite way to say please, literally be good and: Var god och fyll i formuläret.

target: Vi vill att det här fixas snart.
english: We want this to be fixed soon.
tip: Adding -s to a verb makes it passive: fixas means gets fixed, with no helper verb needed.

target: Alla måste följa reglerna.
english: Everyone must follow the rules.
tip: Modal verbs like måste take a plain infinitive with no att: måste följa, never måste att följa.

target: Det finns 365 dagar på ett år.
english: There are 365 days in a year.
tip: "På" used idiomatically: "dagar på ett år" = days in a year.

target: Varje söndagskväll lägger jag ihop tvätten och ställer in den i garderoben.
english: Every Sunday evening I fold the laundry and put it away in the wardrobe.
tip: When a sentence opens with a time phrase, the verb stays second and the subject follows: Varje söndagskväll lägger jag.

target: Jag vore ytterst tacksam i affären.
english: I would be most grateful in business.
tip: "Vore" is subjunctive – extremely polite. Formal letters/requests.

target: Kaffe dricker jag alltid svart.
english: Coffee I always drink black.
tip: Front the object and the verb still stays second, so the subject comes after: Kaffe dricker jag, not Kaffe jag dricker.

target: Ska vi gå ut och äta nog?
english: Shall we go out and eat?
tip: 'Ut' (out) as a particle: 'gå ut' (go out), 'ta ut' (take out), 'se ut' (look/appear).

target: Det var igår som jag träffade henne.
english: It was yesterday that I met her.
tip: Det var X som is a cleft that spotlights one part: Det var igår som jag träffade henne highlights when, not what.

target: Trött som jag var somnade jag direkt.
english: Tired as I was, I fell asleep right away.
tip: Adjective plus som plus subject means as or though: Trött som jag var = tired as I was.

target: Jag vänder mig till er med en fråga.
english: I turn to you with a question.
tip: Vända sig till needs a reflexive matching the subject: Jag vänder mig till er = I approach you.

target: Pengar har vi inte, men tid har vi.
english: Money we don't have, but time we do.
tip: Swedish can move the object to the front for contrast: Pengar har vi inte, men tid har vi means money we lack, but time we have.

target: Han ser fram emot semestern.
english: He looks forward to the vacation.
tip: Se fram emot is a fixed three-word phrase for look forward to: Han ser fram emot semestern.

target: Jag vore tacksam om ni kunde.
english: I would be grateful if you could.
tip: Vore is the subjunctive of vara, used for polite hypotheticals: Jag vore tacksam om ni kunde.

target: Vi anhåller om ert tålamod medan vi utreder ärendet vidare.
english: We request your patience while we investigate the matter further.
tip: Very formal – seen in official notices.

target: Han tänder lampan.
english: He turns on the lamp.
tip: Use tänder for lights, candles and fire; devices like a TV take sätter på instead. Han tänder lampan.

target: Vi räknar ut svaret.
english: We figure out the answer.
tip: The particle ut turns räkna (count) into räkna ut, to work something out or calculate it. Vi räknar ut svaret.

target: Jag fyller i formuläret.
english: I fill in the form.
tip: The particle in fylla i means fill in a form; the i is stressed and never drops. Jag fyller i formuläret.

target: Först då förstod jag.
english: Only then did I understand.
tip: Start a sentence with an adverb and the verb stays in second place, so the subject follows it. Först då förstod jag.

target: Han tar av sig skorna.
english: He takes off his shoes.
tip: Dressing verbs take a reflexive: ta av sig means take off your own clothes, so sig is required. Han tar av sig skorna.

target: Det är alltid trevligt att komma tillbaka hem till Sverige.
english: It is always nice to come back home to Sweden.
tip: 'Tillbaka' (back) as a particle: 'komma tillbaka' (come back), 'ge tillbaka' (give back).

target: Sjunga kan hon verkligen, hon vann talangshown tre år i rad.
english: Sing she really can, she won the talent show three years in a row.
tip: Swedish can place the bare verb first for emphasis: Sjunga kan hon means sing, she really can.
